source_refs.note: PDF 235-236 (book p. 233-234): Theorem 1 (LRT), Figure 8.2, geometric idea, interval of sign change, Example 1 with its sign table

blocks.text: Pichhle page par humne dekha ke root woh jagah hai jahan graph \(x\)-axis ko kaatta hai. Ab sawal yeh hai: agar graph banaye baghair humein yaqeen chahiye ke kisi interval mein root zaroor hai, to kaise maloom karein? Iska jawab ek bohat aasaan magar taqatwar theorem deta hai: Location of Root Theorem (LRT). Yeh is unit ke har method ki buniyaad hai, is liye isay achhi tarah samajh lijiye.

blocks.title: Theorem 1
blocks.text: Maan lijiye \(f\) ek real-valued function hai jo closed interval \([a, b]\) par continuous hai. Agar \(f(a)f(b) < 0\) ho, to \(f\) ka kam az kam ek real root \(c\) open interval \(]a, b[\) mein zaroor hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab theorem ke aakhir mein "open interval \([a, b]\)" likhti hai. Yeh ghalat hai: \([a, b]\) to closed interval hai (dono end points shamil). Open interval \(]a, b[\) hai, jise \((a, b)\) bhi likhte hain (end points shamil nahin). Sahi jumla: "... root \(c\) open interval \(]a, b[\) mein hai." Is ke ilawa "closed interval \([a, b]\)" ke baad full stop bhi reh gaya hai.

blocks.alt: A continuous increasing curve y = f(x). At x = a the point (a, f(a)) is below the x-axis, at x = b the point (b, f(b)) is above it, and the curve crosses the x-axis at c between a and b, where f(c) = 0. Dashed vertical lines join a and b to the curve.
blocks.caption: Figure 8.2: a continuous curve from \((a, f(a))\) below the x-axis to \((b, f(b))\) above it must cross the axis at some \(c\) (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.text: Ab is theorem ka geometric khayal (idea) samajhte hain. Kitab kehti hai: LRT ka idea continuous graph ke rawaiye se aata hai. Agar function interval \([a, b]\) par continuous ho to us ka graph pencil kaghaz se uthaye baghair banaya ja sakta hai. Kyun ke \(f(a)f(b) < 0\) hai, is liye \(f(a)\) aur \(f(b)\) ke sign ulte hain. Bina kisi nuqsan ke maan lete hain ke \(f(a) < 0\) aur \(f(b) > 0\) hai. Is surat mein point \((a, f(a))\) \(x\)-axis ke neeche aur point \((b, f(b))\) \(x\)-axis ke upar hai, jaisa Figure 8.2 mein dikhaya gaya hai. Kyun ke \(f\) \([a, b]\) par continuous hai, graph \((a, f(a))\) se \((b, f(b))\) tak bina kisi jump ya break ke chalta hai, khaas taur par \(x\)-axis par bhi koi toot nahin.

Jab graph \(x\)-axis ke neeche se upar ki taraf jata hai to use kisi point \(c\) par \(x\)-axis ko zaroor kaatna parta hai. Us point par \(f(c) = 0\) hai, yani \(c\) interval mein ek real root hai, aur is se saabit hota hai ke kam az kam ek root zaroor maujood hai. Aise interval \([a, b]\) ko hum function \(f\) ka interval of sign change kehte hain, kyun ke is par function ka sign positive se negative ya negative se positive badalta hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Is theorem ko ek seedhe waade ki tarah parhiye: "continuous + dono kinaron par ulte sign \(\Rightarrow\) beech mein root". Misaal ke taur par socho aap samandar ki satah (sea level) se neeche ek wadi mein khare hain aur sea level se upar pahar ki choti par jana hai, aur raasta kahin se toota hua nahin. To raaste mein kisi na kisi jagah aap bilkul sea level par zaroor honge. Woh jagah root hai.
\(f(a)f(b) < 0\) hi kyun? Product sirf tab negative hota hai jab ek factor negative aur doosra positive ho. To yeh ek test hi bata deta hai ke dono sign ulte hain.
"Kam az kam ek" kyun? Curve \(a\) aur \(b\) ke beech axis ko teen baar (ya koi bhi odd number baar) bhi kaat sakti hai. Theorem ek root ka waada karta hai, bilkul ek ka nahin.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Do baatein jo theorem NAHIN kehta:
1. Continuity ki sharat chhodi nahin ja sakti. \(f(x) = \frac{1}{x}\) mein \(f(-1) = -1\) aur \(f(1) = 1\), yani sign ulte hain, phir bhi \(\frac{1}{x}\) kabhi zero nahin hota. Wajah: \(x = 0\) par graph toot jata hai (jump karta hai), wahan \(f\) continuous nahin.
2. Sign na badle to iska matlab yeh nahin ke root nahin. \(f(x) = x^2 - 4\) mein \(f(-3) = 5\) aur \(f(3) = 5\), dono positive, phir bhi \([-3, 3]\) mein do roots \(\pm 2\) hain. Roots jore mein aaye, is liye kinaron par sign ek jaisa raha.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
\(f(x) = x^3 - 2\) ke liye kya \([1, 2]\) interval of sign change hai?
Jawab: \(f(1) = 1 - 2 = -1 < 0\) aur \(f(2) = 8 - 2 = 6 > 0\). Polynomial hone ki wajah se \(f\) continuous hai, aur \(f(1)f(2) = -6 < 0\). Haan, \([1, 2]\) interval of sign change hai, aur LRT ke mutabiq root (asal mein \(\sqrt[3]{2} \approx 1.26\)) is mein hai.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.problem: Show that the function \(f(x) = x^4 - 200x - 50\) has at least two real roots by finding its intervals of sign change.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = x^4 - 200x - 50\).
Saabit karna: \(f\) ke kam az kam do real roots hain.
Tareeqa: Location of Root Theorem. Agar humein do alag alag closed intervals mil jayen jin par \(f\) continuous ho aur sign badle, to har interval mein kam az kam ek root hoga, yani kul kam az kam do roots.

Continuity
\[\lim_{x \to c} f(x) = \lim_{x \to c}(x^4 - 200x - 50)\]
\[= f(c) \quad \forall c \in \mathbb{R}\]
\[\Rightarrow f \text{ is continuous at every real number.}\]
Kyun: \(f\) polynomial hai, aur polynomial ki limit kisi bhi point par seedha us ki value hoti hai. LRT sirf us interval par lagta hai jahan \(f\) continuous ho, is liye yeh sharat sab se pehle check karte hain.

Interval of sign change: pehli values
\[f(-3) = 81 + 600 - 50\]
\[= 631 > 0\]
\[f(-2) = 16 + 400 - 50\]
\[= 366 > 0\]
Kyun: hum poore numbers (whole numbers) try karte hain kyun ke un ko rakhna aasaan hai.
Dhyan dein: \((-3)^4 = 81\) positive hai (even power), aur \(-200 \times (-3) = +600\), minus minus plus ban jata hai.

Baaqi values (neeche table dekhiye)
\[f(-1) = 1 + 200 - 50 = 151\]
\[f(0) = -50\]
\[f(5) = 625 - 1000 - 50\]
\[= -425\]
\[f(6) = 1296 - 1200 - 50\]
\[= 46\]
Kyun: hum tab tak values nikalte rehte hain jab tak \(f(x)\) ka sign na badle. 0 se 5 tak saari values negative rehti hain; sign wapas + sirf \(x = 6\) par hota hai. Is liye 6 tak jana zaroori tha; agar hum 5 par ruk jate to doosra root nazar hi na aata.

Sign kahan badla?
\[f(-1)\,f(0) = (151)(-50) < 0\]
\[f(5)\,f(6) = (-425)(46) < 0\]
Kyun: do numbers ka product negative tabhi hota hai jab un ke sign ulte hon. Is liye \([-1, 0]\) aur \([5, 6]\) dono \(f\) ke intervals of sign change hain.

LRT se nateeja
LRT ke mutabiq ek root \(]-1, 0[\) mein hai aur ek root \(]5, 6[\) mein.
Kyun: dono intervals par \(f\) continuous hai aur dono par sign badalta hai. Dono intervals aapas mein overlap nahin karte, is liye yeh do mukhtalif roots hain. Yani \(f\) ke kam az kam do real roots hain.

Tasdeeq:
\[\text{Roots} \approx -0.2500 \text{ and } 5.9291\]
Kyun: computer se roots nikalein to yahi do real roots aate hain, aur waqai \(-0.25 \in\, ]-1, 0[\) aur \(5.93 \in\, ]5, 6[\). Yani hamara nateeja bilkul durust hai.
blocks.answer: \([-1, 0]\) aur \([5, 6]\) continuous function \(f\) ke intervals of sign change hain, is liye LRT ke mutabiq \(f(x) = x^4 - 200x - 50\) ke kam az kam do real roots hain. Saabit ho gaya.

blocks.caption: Values of \(f(x) = x^4 - 200x - 50\) (the table printed in Example 1)

blocks.text: Kitab aakhir mein yeh kehti hai: \(f(-1)f(0) < 0\), yani \([-1, 0]\) \(f\) ka interval of sign change hai. Isi tarah \(f(5)f(6) < 0\), to \([5, 6]\) doosra interval of sign change hai. Humne \(f\) ke do intervals of sign change dikha diye. Kyun ke \(f\) in intervals par continuous hai, is ke kam az kam do real roots hain.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text: (Yeh hamari misaal hai, kitab ki nahin.) \(f(x) = x^2 - 5\) lijiye. Whole numbers par values: \(f(-3) = 4\), \(f(-2) = -1\), \(f(2) = -1\), \(f(3) = 4\). Sign table: +, −, −, +. Sign do jagah badla: \([-3, -2]\) aur \([2, 3]\) mein. To LRT ke mutabiq do roots hain, aur waqai roots \(\pm\sqrt{5} \approx \pm 2.236\) hain, jo bilkul inhi intervals mein hain.

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text:
Intervals of sign change jaldi dhoondne ka tareeqa:
1. Whole numbers (\(\ldots, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, \ldots\)) par \(f(x)\) ki table banaiye.
2. Har value ke neeche sirf us ka sign likhiye.
3. Jahan bhi sign palte (+ se − ya − se +), wahan ek interval of sign change hai.
Exam mein hamesha continuity wali line, dono values un ke sign ke saath, aur yeh jumla "hence by the LRT a root lies in ..." zaroor likhiye; in teeno ke marks hote hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Example 1 mein ek baat bohat ghaur talab hai. Agar hum sirf \(-3\) se \(3\) tak values dekhte, to sirf ek sign change milta, \([-1, 0]\) wala, aur hum samajhte ke root ek hi hai. Doosra root \(5\) aur \(6\) ke beech chhupa hua tha, kyun ke \(-200x\) wala term \(x^4\) par kaafi der tak bhaari rehta hai. \(x^4\) us waqt jeet-ta hai jab \(x\) kaafi bara ho jaye. Sabaq yeh hai: table itni lambi banaiye ke function ka poora rawaiya (behaviour) samajh aa jaye, aur bari power wale term ko yaad rakhiye, kyun ke aakhir mein wahi faisla karta hai ke graph upar jayega ya neeche.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
\(f(x) = x^4 - 200x - 50\) ke liye kya hum yaqeen se keh sakte hain ke is ke bilkul do hi real roots hain?
Jawab: LRT sirf "kam az kam do" kehta hai. Bilkul do ka saboot LRT se nahin milta; us ke liye derivative se function ka rawaiya dekhna parta hai (\(f'(x) = 4x^3 - 200\) sirf ek jagah zero hota hai, to graph pehle neeche aata hai aur phir upar jata hai, yani do se zyada crossings nahin). Computer bhi do hi real roots deta hai. Exam mein sirf wohi likhiye jo sawal poochta hai: "at least two".

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text: (Yeh hamari misaal hai, kitab ki nahin.) Socho subah ka thermometer \(-2^{\circ}\)C dikha raha tha aur dopehar ko \(+5^{\circ}\)C. Temperature achanak chhalaang nahin lagata, aahista aahista badalta hai (yani continuous hai). To beech mein kisi waqt temperature bilkul \(0^{\circ}\)C zaroor hua hoga, chahe humne us lamhe ko dekha ho ya nahin. LRT yahi baat functions ke liye kehta hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Notation ka chhota sa farq yaad kar lijiye: \([a, b]\) closed interval hai, jis mein \(a\) aur \(b\) khud shamil hain. \(]a, b[\) open interval hai, jis mein \(a\) aur \(b\) shamil nahin. Root open interval mein isliye hai ke \(f(a)\) aur \(f(b)\) to zero nahin (ek negative aur ek positive hai), is liye root kinaron par ho hi nahin sakta; woh beech mein kahin hai.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Location of Root Theorem: agar \(f\) \([a, b]\) par continuous ho aur \(f(a)f(b) < 0\), to \(f\) ka kam az kam ek real root \(c\) \(]a, b[\) mein hai.
2. Aise \([a, b]\) ko \(f\) ka interval of sign change kehte hain.
3. Hamesha pehle continuity check kijiye, phir \(f(a)\) aur \(f(b)\) ke sign milaiye.
4. Alag alag (overlap na karne wale) intervals of sign change alag alag roots dete hain; \(k\) aise intervals ka matlab kam az kam \(k\) roots.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. LRT aise interval par lagana jahan \(f\) continuous nahin (jaise \(\frac{1}{x}\) ya \(\tan x\) ke asymptote ke aar paar). Wahan sign badalne se root saabit nahin hota.
2. \(f(a)\) aur \(f(b)\) ka sign ek jaisa dekh kar "koi root nahin" keh dena. Beech mein do roots (ya koi bhi nahin) ho sakte hain.
3. Yeh kehna ke LRT bilkul ek root deta hai. Woh kam az kam ek ki zamanat deta hai.
4. Negative numbers mein sign ki ghalti: \((-3)^4 = +81\) aur \(-200 \times (-3) = +600\).
